text: The tool deliberately requires ESPHome 2026.1 or newer. When the entity-name web API URLs replaced object-id URLs, we considered supporting both schemes behind a version probe so older firmware kept working. The user was asked directly and said they do not care about older ESPHome, so the dual code path was dropped rather than written. Do not add a compatibility shim back without asking: the reason is a product decision, not an oversight. Note that object-id URLs still function today and only stop working in ESPHome 2026.7.0, so a future report of 404s on every write from someone on old firmware is expected behaviour, not a regression.

The threshold margin (default 10 above the empty-room peak) is set on the results page, not on the setup form or in the URL. The user rejected the setup-form placement: the margin only matters when proposals are computed, so there is no need to carry it through connect and the measurement phases. Recomputing proposals in the browser was also rejected: it would duplicate propose_threshold in JavaScript and leave the tight / no detection labels stale. The server recomputes on POST /margin and stays the single source of the rule. Context: the walk and still phases are mostly diagnostic; the proposed value is empty_max + margin except in the tight case, which is why skipping them after the empty phase was added.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The device YAML (esphome-configs/presence_sensor.yaml) sets filters: [] and state_topic: null on the 18 ld2410 gate energy sensors. Reason, observed by the user: after calibration, presence flickered in an empty room. Cause: ESPHome's default throttle_with_priority: 1000ms on ld2410 sensors let the calibrator see about one radar frame in ten during the empty phase, so the measured peaks and the written thresholds were too low. The calibrator now shows the peak per-sensor publish rate on the results page and warns at 1.5/s or below. Rejected: throttle: 100ms (adds nothing over no filter at a 10 Hz frame rate) and 200ms (drops half the frames, including peaks). The gate energies were taken off MQTT because nothing downstream reads them and the C3 would otherwise push up to 180 messages/s during a session.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The tool requires ESPHome 2026.8 or newer, superseding the earlier 2026.1 floor (entry jcfunp). 2026.8.0 (esphome#17586, breaking) changed the web server SSE payload: 'id' became the entity-name path ('sensor/Office Gate 3 Move Energy'), 'name_id' was dropped, and 'domain' appears only in the initial dump. Observed as KeyError('name_id') and a connect loop right after the user reflashed with 2026.8. Decision: adopt the new shape only, no dual-shape support or version probe, consistent with the earlier choice not to carry old firmware.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>
